adaptive_step_adaptive_phase_correlation.statement: same scenario, same noisy data, with adaptive_step=True (zuo2016's Eq. 16 rule) instead of the fixed ramp -- a real, reproducible improvement at this noise level, validated across 8 random seeds (8/8 favored adaptive_step, not itself in this registry since a multi-seed statistic isn't a single deterministic number)

adaptive_step_fixed_ramp_phase_correlati.statement: phase_correlation with the default fixed exponential-ramp step schedule, at heavy Poisson noise (peak_photon_count=3) and 400 iterations -- enough noise/cycles for zuo2016's described failure mode to manifest (an earlier pass at lighter noise and fewer iterations found no clean difference)

epry_corrected_phase_correlation.statement: same scenario, reconstructed with EPRY pupil recovery (recover_pupil=True) instead of assuming the ideal pupil -- a real but modest improvement, not a full fix

epry_paper_scale_baseline_phase_correlat.statement: same no-aberration scenario as epry_small_scale_*, but at a scale close to ou2014's own real demonstration (225 LEDs, 64x64px instead of 12x12, object spatial frequency kept physically comparable)

epry_paper_scale_corrected_phase_correla.statement: same paper-scale scenario, with recover_pupil=True -- the small-scale regression does NOT reproduce here, confirming it is a small-testbed/low-data-redundancy artifact, not a general EPRY failure or an implementation bug

epry_recovered_pupil_phase_correlation.statement: correlation between the EPRY-recovered pupil's phase and the true injected aberration's phase -- confirms EPRY identifies the actual aberration, not just 'helps the object by coincidence'

epry_small_scale_baseline_phase_correlat.statement: phase_correlation for the blue (470nm) channel on this project's small 9x9-LED/12x12px synthetic testbed, NO aberration present (ideal pupil) -- already reconstructs well without any pupil correction

epry_small_scale_corrected_phase_correla.statement: same scenario, with recover_pupil=True -- EPRY REGRESSES this already-healthy channel at this small testbed scale, even with no real aberration to correct

epry_uncorrected_phase_correlation.statement: phase_correlation assuming the ideal (unaberrated) pupil, when a real defocus aberration (Zernike mode 4, ou2014's own dominant real-microscope aberration) is actually present in the optics

five_percent_contrast_object_phase_corre.statement: reconstruction phase_correlation for the SAME phase field with just 5% amplitude contrast added -- demonstrates how much a small amount of amplitude structure matters to this solver

led_calibration_scale_recovery_error.statement: absolute error between the LED spectral-correlation calibration's fitted scale factor and a known injected misalignment's true scale factor, given a good object spectrum estimate

multispectral_thickness_correlation.detail: see tests/test_multispectral_end_to_end.py for the identical scenario as an assertion
multispectral_thickness_correlation.statement: correlation between the milestone-2 coupled pipeline's recovered sample-thickness field and the true field, on a synthetic 3-channel dispersion object reconstructed through the actual Wirtinger flow solver (not injected phase)

phase_only_object_phase_correlation.statement: reconstruction phase_correlation for a UNIFORM-amplitude (pure phase) object -- the baseline solver's known weak point, see docs/roadmap_agentic_multispectral_pipeline.md section 1 point 6

ransac_plain_fit_rotation_error_rad.statement: absolute rotation error (radians) of a plain least-squares similarity-transform fit with 10% of points corrupted to implausible positions

ransac_robust_fit_rotation_error_rad.statement: same scenario, same points, fit with fit_similarity_transform_ransac instead -- the outlier-rejection improvement added to LED calibration

suite_coverage.statement: checks.py pass/fail coverage for this project's correctness suite

tie_informed_init_baseline_phase_correla.statement: phase_correlation for a mixed-low/high-spatial-frequency phase object with the default zero-phase solver initialization

tie_informed_init_phase_correlation.statement: phase_correlation for the SAME object, initializing the solver with a Transport of Intensity Equation phase estimate instead of zero -- fixes the degenerate saddle point found in docs/roadmap_agentic_multispectral_pipeline.md section 1 point 6

unwrapping_error_reduction_factor.statement: how many times smaller the coupled (unwrap + dispersion-fit) pipeline's thickness RMSE is than a naive baseline that treats each channel's raw wrapped phase as already-unwrapped OPL, on a synthetic dispersion signal large enough to require real unwrapping
